metadata.title: Technology-related knowledge, skills, and attitudes of pre- and in-service teachers: The current situation and emerging trends

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This article is an introductory special-issue overview and does not conduct an empirical large-scale assessment analysis with student microdata. Therefore, no sampling frame, school/student selection, or complex survey weighting (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) is specified or applied. For future empirical work using ILSA microdata (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIAAC), analysts should use the provided student sampling weights and replicate weights (if available) to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors under the complex design. The present paper instead synthesizes prior research and outlines conceptual and assessment-related considerations for technology-related teacher KSA.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values (PV) are generated for cognitive achievement scales in ILSA student assessments (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIAAC). This paper does not analyze any ILSA student achievement outcomes with PVs; it is a conceptual/overview article about technology-related teacher knowledge, skills, and attitudes (KSA) and how such constructs are assessed and fostered. Because there is no PV-based dependent variable and no empirical ILSA microdata analysis, PV handling is not applicable and missing-data handling for PV estimation is not reported.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No ILSA microdata sample is analyzed. The paper summarizes and contextualizes findings from multiple studies (including references to large-scale studies such as PIAAC and TALIS) but does not report an analytic dataset, inclusion/exclusion criteria, or an original participant sample for the present article.

data.outcome_summary: This article is an introductory overview for a special issue on technology-related knowledge, skills, and attitudes (KSA) of pre- and in-service teachers. It does not perform an original empirical analysis with a defined ILSA dataset/cycle, nor does it train or evaluate machine-learning models on ILSA microdata. Instead, it specifies the conceptual basis (notably the TPACK framework), reviews how technology-related KSA are assessed (self-assessment vs. external/objective measures), and outlines directions for fostering these KSA, including future-oriented considerations such as artificial intelligence and “augmentation strategies.” Because no student-level achievement outcomes are modeled, there are no PV-based benchmarks, no reported predictive metrics (e.g., AUC/RMSE), and no sampling/weighting or missing-data procedures for an analytic dataset. Consequently, the contribution is methodological and conceptual rather than results-driven.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the article is not an empirical large-scale assessment study with an analytic sample, outcome variable, and ML pipeline. It functions as a conceptual introduction and synthesis of prior work across multiple studies and contexts, so fields such as total sample size, country-level Ns, PV handling, missing-data handling, and ML model performance are not applicable to this paper’s own analysis. The paper also does not provide a results section with predictive metrics that could be mapped to StructuredFinding rows.
